Messages.Author: Jorge Ramírez
Messages.Body:
First of all I have to say that in the EC and the Austrian Qualifier,
the organization team from Vienna did a great work, LSJ as White Wolf
representative too. Organization was excellent and the place choosen
for the event was great. I think that the record of players in a
tournament was beaten (115 players).

The only one problem "shadowing" the event happened in the Austrian
Qualifier finals at Saturday. I played the tournament, I was there,
very near. I was sitted at two metters from the judges when the
decklists of the two french players at the final where revised. This
is what happened:

1.- Before the final begins, the judges ask all 5 players to give
their decks for revision. I am sitting just at two meters from the
judges while they check the decks against the official decklist given.

2.- Two diferent judges find differences in the decks of the two
french finalists. To be concrect: Stephane Lavrut decklist for the
tournament said "3 Direct intervention and 3 Memories of moratility",
the judges found 4 memories of mortality and 2 direct intervention.
One of the memories of mortality was from a different edition than the
other three, and the sleeve of this card was absolutely brilliant and
new (making clear that he could have putted it in the deck DURING the
tournament).
In the other hand the other french finalist also had differences
beetween the number of Blur/pursuits writen and his deck (I could not
hear exactly the difference, but THERE was a difference).

3.- Organizators & judges talk and read the V:EKN tournament rules for
this case and it is clear: DISQUALIFICATION. Worried about the strict
consecuences, they ask LSJ, who confirms that rules say. Being
reasonable, before taking the final decision, they decide to ask the
players for the difference.

First time asqued, Stephane Lavrut says that "may be, the fourth
Memories of Mortality was put inside my deck from other player's deck
in previous rounds". The judges ask then, where is the third direct
intervention?. Then there is a lot of confussion and weak explanations
and finally the french player says that he, from the beginning was
playing with 4 MoM and 2 DI. When the judges print his decklist with
the 3 MoM and the 3 DI, he brings a piece of paper printed and
MODIFIED WITH A PENCIL and begin to swear that he mistaked in the
decklist and that he bought the deck written from home with 4 MoM and
2 DI.

4.- The judges, finally resolve to allow them to play the finals with
a severe warning (I think they did this because if they would have
disqualified the two french players, all the tournament and next day
EC would have been modified, and time was 20:00 before starting the
finals).

5.- The two French players start to play in the finals. This was the
table order:

- The Lasombra (Jeff) with a Lasombra/Embrace deck (It was great
Jeff!!!)
- An UK player with a Stanislava Bleed + Prot deck (Interesting, I
played against him in the last round of the EC)
- The second French player (not Stephan) with a CEL + Guns + Rush
Brujah Deck
- Stephane Lavrut with Turbo tzimisce War Ghoul Deck.
- An Euro Brujah Deck (I don't remember the nacionality of the player)

6.- After 12 turns, the first French player (guns + cel) had not did a
single bleed or rush agaist his prey (second French Player: Stephan).
He was all the time crying because "he was going to die" because of
the Anarch Revolts of the lasombra (he had 15 pool, 4 vampires,
Powerbase montreal and Hunting ground/blood doll). Meanwhile, his prey
(Stephane), brings out 3 war ghouls, and outs his prey (the
eurobrujah). Jeff does the same with the Stanyslava UK deck, and still
then, NOT A SINGLE BLEED OR RUSH AGAINST HIS PREY (STEPHANE). Then,
Stephane Lavrut begins to talk with the brujah FOR HIM TO RUSH THE
LASOMBRA VAMPIRES!!! in order to get the finals VP's.

7.- The judges warns the brujah player for his play mode, the Brujah
player make a small bleed for the judge, and finally the Tzimisce outs
the Lasombra.

8.- Once the two Frenchs where alone in the table, IN 3 TURNS, the
brujah deck destroys ALL the WarGhouls of Stephan, and sends ALL his
vampires into torpor and wins the only VP necessary to be the 2nd
qualified.

This is what happened. I am Jorge Ramirez, from Spain, I played the
Austrian Qualifier (I got there the EC Qualification) and the EC
tournament on sunday (I was 10th) . I have seen this by myself, nobody
has told this information to me, and this is real.

I understand the position of the judges, this is very difficult to
avoid. But it is sad that the two players wich had wrong decklists,
played this way in the finals after they where given the oportunity to
play instead of desqualification.

Messages.Author: John Keech
Messages.Body:
"Jorge Ramírez" <jo...@r2sistemas.com> wrote in message
news:535e0619.02120...@posting.google.com

*Snip the long report etc*

> I understand the position of the judges, this is very difficult to
> avoid. But it is sad that the two players wich had wrong decklists,
> played this way in the finals after they where given the oportunity to
> play instead of desqualification.

This seems to be a fair and reasonable account of what happened. The
judges made their decision and the players played their game. The game
is done, the result stands, and it has been discussed to death. I think
Jeff (The Lasombra) videoed the whole match, and it should appear on his
website for those who are still interested in going over the past.

As far as I know, the vast majority of the players (and it wasn't like
there weren't many after all) had a really good time, and the
organisation was really good considering that there were four separate
tournaments played in two days. This is not to mention the organisation
that went into the welcoming party and the LARP display that went on
there (someone really should have tried to claim the two good luck
charms that no-one owned up to, especially as one of the clans that were
not 'defended' won the EC). Well done Carl and the crew.

Can we talk about something else now? It's not like anything is going
to be changed - it's all a bit late for recriminations isn't it?

--
